note: Protected Forms is a spam filter with no plugins/Drush. Config object protected_forms.settings has everything under a nested 'protected_forms' mapping: allowed_scripts (seq), check_quantity (int), reject_message (text), reject_patterns (comma/newline list), log_rejected (bool), allowed_patterns (string), excluded_forms (seq). Admin route protected_forms.admin at /admin/config/content/protected_forms; permissions 'administer protected forms' and 'bypass protected forms validation'. It adds _protected_forms_validate via hook_form_alter to non-admin, non-delete forms whose id contains user_/node_/comment_/contact_message_/webform_ or equals private_message_add_form. Rejected count is State protected_forms.rejected; rejections log to the 'protected forms' dblog channel. Medium/hard are grounded in the real config object (check_quantity, allowed_scripts, excluded_forms); cleanups restore the shipped config/install defaults explicitly.

evals.prompt: For the Drupal protected_forms module, which config object stores its settings, and which setting holds the list of spam words/patterns that cause a submission to be rejected?
evals.expected_output: Settings live in protected_forms.settings (nested under a 'protected_forms' mapping). The spam list is reject_patterns, a comma/newline-separated list of words and URL schemes; a submission is rejected if any pattern matches.

evals.prompt: Which forms does protected_forms validate by default, and how can a trusted role skip the spam checks?
evals.expected_output: It validates non-admin, non-delete forms whose id contains user_, node_, comment_, contact_message_, or webform_ (and private_message_add_form). A role with the 'bypass protected forms validation' permission skips all checks; forms listed in excluded_forms are also skipped.

evals.prompt: Besides matching bad words, how does protected_forms block foreign-language spam, and which setting controls that? What setting limits how much of the text it samples?
evals.expected_output: It samples up to check_quantity random characters and rejects the submission if any character belongs to a Unicode script not listed in allowed_scripts (e.g. Latin-only sites block Cyrillic/CJK). allowed_scripts is the allowlist; check_quantity is the sample size.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, protected_forms is configured. Inspect the live configuration and state how many characters it samples for the language-script check (the check_quantity value).
evals.expected_output: check_quantity is 42: protected_forms.settings -> protected_forms.check_quantity = 42. Read it with drush cget protected_forms.settings protected_forms.check_quantity.

evals.prompt: Inspect the live protected_forms configuration on this site and list the Unicode language scripts it currently allows in form submissions.
evals.expected_output: allowed_scripts is [Currency Symbols, Latin, Miscellaneous Symbols, Cyrillic] — notably Cyrillic has been added beyond the shipped defaults. Found at protected_forms.settings -> protected_forms.allowed_scripts.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure protected_forms so that the form with id 'pf_custom_form' is exempt from its spam validation (i.e. add it to the module's excluded forms). Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: protected_forms.settings -> protected_forms.excluded_forms now contains 'pf_custom_form' (in addition to whatever was there). E.g. load the config, push 'pf_custom_form' onto the excluded_forms array, and save.

evals.prompt: The spam filter on my site is blocking one of my own forms (its id is 'pf_custom_form'). Please tell the Protected Forms spam checker to leave that particular form alone, and save it on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add 'pf_custom_form' to protected_forms.settings -> protected_forms.excluded_forms and save so that form skips validation.
